claims.statement: Laws of Gaozu and Taizong were barely preserved in later ages

From Gaozong and Empress Wu onward poison flowed through the realm; Tang mandate severed and renewed
From Suzong onward almost nothing worth recording on penal law remained
After Yizong there was nothing worth praising on penal law
Later sovereigns no longer possessed Taizong's aspiration

translationRepairs: In the fourth year Gaozu personally reviewed prisoners. Because many had broken the law amid the turmoil, he pardoned all except robbers who injured their victims, deserters from military service, and officials who had perverted justice.

In the fourth year Gaozu personally reviewed prisoners. Because many had broken the law amid the turmoil, he pardoned theft that was not robbery injuring the owner, deserters from military service, and officials who had perverted the law.
皆原之 pardons the listed classes: 盜非劫傷其主, 征人逃亡, and 官吏枉法. The before text wrongly turns them into exceptions; the proposed after matches the Chinese and the literal.
Afterward he again ordered the Vice Director Pei Ji and fifteen others to compile the code and ordinances anew; the code in all had five hundred articles, supplemented by fifty-three articles.

Afterward he again ordered Vice Director Pei Ji and others, fifteen persons in all, to compile the code and ordinances anew; the code in all had five hundred articles, supplemented by fifty-three articles.
僕射裴寂等十五人 is a total of fifteen including Pei Ji, so “fifteen others” is wrong; the proposed “a group of fifteen in all” is still awkward English, so restate the inclusive count clearly.
How can one commit the lightest punishment and yet sometimes die?"
How can one incur the lightest punishment and yet sometimes die?"
犯至輕之刑 is to incur or undergo the lightest punishment; “commit the … punishment” misreads 犯 with 刑 as the object.
Capital prisoners were reported monthly to the Ministry of Justice, and censors conducted inspections.
Capital prisoners were reported monthly by the Ministry of Justice, and censors conducted inspections.
刑部月一奏 makes the Ministry of Justice the agent that memorializes monthly about capital prisoners, not the recipient of reports.
Officials of fifth rank and above rode to the place of execution under supervision of the Court of Judicial Review, or were granted death at home.
Officials of fifth rank and above rode to the place of execution under supervision of the Director of the Court of Judicial Review, or were granted death at home.
大理正 names the Director of the Court of Judicial Review as supervisor; omitting 正 understates the office.
After Zhang Jungu's death, however, judges treated lenient misjudgment as the cautionary lesson, while harsh misjudgment went unpunished—and from that point the law grew gradually stricter.
After Zhang Yungu's death, however, judges treated lenient misjudgment as the cautionary lesson, while harsh misjudgment went unpunished—and from that point the law grew gradually stricter.
張蘊古 is Zhang Yungu, as earlier in the chapter; Jungu is a bad reading of 蘊古.

Yet from the death of Zhang Jungu onward, judicial officials took erroneous leniency as a warning; when there was erroneous severity, no penalty was imposed—from this the clerical law gradually tightened.

Yet from the death of Zhang Yungu onward, judicial officials took erroneous leniency as a warning; when there was erroneous severity, no penalty was imposed—from this the clerical law gradually tightened.
The same 張蘊古 requires Zhang Yungu in the literal field; Jungu is the parallel transliteration error.
In Kaiyuan 3, Yellow Gate Commissioner Lu Huai-shen and others compiled the Kaiyuan Administrative Rules.
In Kaiyuan 3 under Xuanzong, Yellow Gate Commissioner Lu Huaishen and others compiled the Kaiyuan Administrative Rules.
玄宗開元三年 requires naming Xuanzong, and 盧懷慎 is Lu Huaishen without a hyphenated given name.

Under Emperor Xuanzong, Left Guard Command warehouse clerk Zhang Cui arranged the penal code by category, appended administrative edicts, and compiled the Dazhong Unified Categories of Penal Law; the Ministry of Justice was ordered to promulgate it.

Under Emperor Xuānzong, Left Guard Command warehouse clerk Zhang Kui arranged the penal code by category, appended administrative edicts, and compiled the Dazhong Unified Categories of Penal Law; the Ministry of Justice was ordered to promulgate it.
宣宗 is Xuānzong, distinct from 玄宗, and 張戣 is Zhang Kui; Cui and undiacriticized Xuanzong alone conflate persons and misread the given name.

In Emperor Xuanzong's time, Warehouse Clerk of the Left Guard Command Zhang Cui classified the penal code into categories, appended administrative edicts, and produced the Dazhong Unified Categories of Penal Law; an edict ordered the Ministry of Justice to promulgate it.

In Emperor Xuānzong's time, Warehouse Clerk of the Left Guard Command Zhang Kui classified the penal code into categories, appended administrative edicts, and produced the Dazhong Unified Categories of Penal Law; an edict ordered the Ministry of Justice to promulgate it.
The literal has the same 宣宗/張戣 errors; Xuānzong and Zhang Kui restore the Chinese names.
After Xu Jingye, Prince of Yue Zhen, Prince of Langye Chong, and others raised armies against her, the Wu clan grew even more fearful.
After Xu Jingye, Zhen the Prince of Yue, Chong the Prince of Langye, and others raised armies against her, the Wu clan grew even more fearful.
越王貞 and 琅邪王沖 are Zhen, Prince of Yue, and Chong, Prince of Langye; “Prince of Yue Zhen” fuses title and personal name.
Interrogators treat harsh severity as merit, inventing charges from nothing to outdo one another, each boasting of the other's cruelty.
Interrogators treat harsh severity as merit, inventing charges from nothing to outdo one another, each vaunting cruelty.
相矜以虐 means they mutually boast by means of cruelty, not that each boasts of the other’s cruelty.

The notorious bandit Gao Yu gathered followers on South Mountain and killed several thousand people. After he was captured, an amnesty was proclaimed. Daizong was inclined to spare his life, but the chief ministers argued he should be dismembered and salted. The emperor did not consent, yet in the end Gao Yu was beaten to death.

The notorious bandit Gao Yu gathered followers on South Mountain and devoured several thousand people. After he was captured, an amnesty was proclaimed. Daizong was inclined to spare his life, but the chief ministers argued he should be dismembered and salted. The emperor did not consent, yet in the end Gao Yu was beaten to death.
啗人數千 is cannibalistic devouring, so “killed” is too weak; “ate” is semantically right but less natural than “devoured,” which matches the source verb and the existing literal.
Considering their wholehearted devotion and compassion for all beneath Heaven, they may truly be called benevolent!
Considering their wholehearted devotion and compassion for others, they may truly be called benevolent!
推心惻物 has compassion for creatures/others only; “all beneath Heaven” is invented.

Minister of Works Yu Di also urged the emperor to use harsh punishments to recover sovereign authority. The emperor told the chancellors, "Di harbors treacherous designs and wants me to lose the people's hearts."

Minister of Works Yu Di also urged the emperor to use punishments to recover sovereign authority. The emperor told the chancellors, "Di harbors treacherous designs and wants me to lose the people's hearts."
用刑 means use punishments; the Chinese does not add 重/酷, so “harsh” is an unsupported intensifier.
